title: Proof Chain — Principal Signs, Notary Countersigns
note: When `proof` is an array it is a W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0 proof chain — a facility the data model already defines, not an APH invention — of exactly two: the principal proof (proof_purpose "assertionMethod", the human's key, the actual authorization) then the notary countersignature (proof_purpose "authentication", covering the COMPLETE principal proof). Each proof covers the document plus every proof BEFORE it and nothing after, so the principal's base is the envelope carrying its proof ALONE — a signer cannot sign bytes that do not exist yet. That fixes the issuance order: the notary prepares the envelope, the principal signs it, the notary countersigns. `previous_proof` is what makes the chain a chain: array order is a hint an intermediary can rearrange, so the notary proof names the principal proof's `id` and the verifier checks that binding. Verify in chain order, and reject any envelope whose declared `attestation_mode` disagrees with its proof structure — the label is not evidence.
book_ref: APH Spec: §7.1.11 EnvelopeProof, §7.2.1 Canonicalization base per proof, §8.3.1 Verifying a proof chain
